title: Creating a
*Class*
ytTitle: Pascal 16.1 - Creating a Class: plan it in UML, code it in Lazarus
desc:
What is a class, and why does your program want one? Starting from one game in a library of games, we work out what we need to know about it and what we want to do with it, plan the class in UML, then code it in Lazarus with the plan beside the code - typing every End straight away and every function's Result := first.

Download the code (Lazarus project, zip):
https://bestlessons.co.za/downloads/tutorials/pascal-16.1-creating-a-class.zip

In this video:
- A class = data + the procedures and functions that work on it (methods)
- Access modifiers: private and public
- Planning the class as a UML class diagram
- Constructor, destructor, getters and setters, ToString and a helper method
- The class in its own unit (uClassGame), and Ctrl+Shift+C
- Objects, dot notation, and why private really is private

title: An Array
*Manager*
Class
ytTitle: Pascal 20.1 - An Array Manager Class: think it, plan it, code it (search, best, total, sort)
desc:
A whole library of games in one object. We plan an array manager class in UML, then work out each job by hand - adding, searching, the best, the total, swapping and a selection sort - draw it as a flowchart, and turn each flowchart into code in Lazarus, with the flowchart beside the code.

Download the code (Lazarus project, zip):
https://bestlessons.co.za/downloads/tutorials/pascal-20.1-array-manager.zip

In this video:
- An array manager: the array, the number of objects in it, and the methods that look after them
- Who owns the objects - and freeing them all in the destructor
- A constant for the array's size (MAX_GAMES)
- Adding, with a check for a full shelf
- A linear search that stops when it finds the game, ignoring capitals
- Finding the best, and adding up a total
- Swapping two objects, and a selection sort
- The main program that uses the shelf

title: Text File
*Basics*
ytTitle: Pascal 17.1 - Text File Basics: write, add to and read a text file
desc:
Programs forget everything when they close - unless they write it to a file. We work out what a text file is, plan writing and reading as flowcharts, then code it in Lazarus: AssignFile, Rewrite, Append, Reset, Readln while Not Eof, FileExists, and why CloseFile matters.

Download the code (Lazarus project, zip):
https://bestlessons.co.za/downloads/tutorials/pascal-17.1-text-files.zip

In this video:
- Why variables forget, and what persistence means
- A TextFile variable, tied to a name with AssignFile
- Rewrite, Append and Reset - three ways to open a file
- Why CloseFile matters: the buffer
- Reading to the end of the file with Eof
- Checking the file is there with FileExists

title: Where's the
*File?*
ytTitle: Pascal 17.2 - Where's the File? Runtime error 2, hidden extensions and the program's folder
desc:
"Runtime error 2 - file not found" - but the file is right there! The three usual reasons: the wrong folder, a hidden extension (games.txt.txt), and a program started from somewhere else. We plan a program that checks first, make the file, find the hidden extension, and use ExtractFilePath (ParamStr (0)) to find files next to the program.

Download the code (Lazarus project, zip):
https://bestlessons.co.za/downloads/tutorials/pascal-17.2-where-is-the-file.zip

In this video:
- A file name with no folder means the current folder
- From Lazarus, that's the project's folder
- FileExists before you read
- Hidden extensions, and how to switch them on
- ExtractFilePath (ParamStr (0)): the program's own folder

- Parsing by hand: find the comma, copy what's before it, cut both off
- Pos, Copy and Delete
- Text from a file is text: StrToFloat and StrToInt
- Why there must be no spaces around the commas

title: A Game on
a *Line*
ytTitle: Pascal 17.4 - A Game on a Line: Create (aLine) and StringForFile
desc:
A class should know its own format. We give the game class from Pascal 16.1 two new jobs: a second constructor, Create (aLine), that fills a game in from one line of a file (through a private ParseLine helper and the setters), and StringForFile, which gives the game back as one line for the file. Then a test program writes two games to a file and reads them back.

Download the code (Lazarus project, zip):
https://bestlessons.co.za/downloads/tutorials/pascal-17.4-a-game-on-a-line.zip

In this video:
- Why the parsing goes in the class
- Two directions: a line becomes a game, a game becomes a line
- StringForFile is not ToString
- Two constructors with one name: Overload
- A private helper, ParseLine, that uses the setters
- Ctrl + click to jump to where something is made

title: Saving the
*Shelf*
ytTitle: Pascal 20.2 - Saving and Loading the Shelf: SaveToFile and LoadFromFile
desc:
A shelf of games that remembers. Our array manager forgets everything when the program closes, so we give it two new methods: SaveToFile, which writes one line for every game, and LoadFromFile, which reads the file back and makes a game from each line. We plan the file first, work out each job on the board, draw it as a flowchart, then code it in Lazarus with the flowchart beside the code. Then we add a game to the file by hand and load it.

Download the code (Lazarus project, zip):
https://bestlessons.co.za/downloads/tutorials/pascal-20.2-saving-the-shelf.zip

In this video:
- Planning the file: one game on each line, its fields separated by commas
- Who makes the line? The game does (StringForFile)
- SaveToFile: Rewrite, a loop, CloseFile
- LoadFromFile: a Boolean answer - was the file there?
- Each line becomes a game (Create with a line), with Trim and a check for empty lines
- A program that loads, sorts, shows and saves the shelf
- Adding a game to the file by hand
